verdict.rationale: Smithery's own docs describe a publishing flow for remote servers (by URL) and for local stdio servers (as a distributed MCPB bundle). Published servers get a dedicated page where users can discover, try and install them, with deep-link auto-configuration, and the CLI can search the registry. An independent community scan of the top 100 registry servers confirms third-party servers are actually distributed there. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of the publishing workflow itself, plus detail on review or moderation steps in the publish flow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can publish my own MCP server on the platform for distribution, discovery, and installation by others

citations.quote: If you’ve already deployed an MCP server elsewhere, you can publish it directly on Smithery via the URL method.
For local stdio servers — Smithery distributes a pre-built MCPB bundle that clients download and run locally.
Distribution — Get a dedicated server page where users can discover, try, and install your MCP from any client
When a user clicks a deep link from our server page, the client automatically configures the MCP with the correct settings.
smithery mcp search [term]              # Search the Smithery registry
